title: Smoothness at a prime descends along a field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $K$ a field extension of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension] and $S$ a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $S_K=K\otimes_kS$, a $K$-algebra through $\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes1$, with the ring map $j:S\to S_K$, $s\mapsto1\otimes s$. Let $\mathfrak q_K\subset S_K$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak q=j^{-1}(\mathfrak q_K)$, a prime ideal of $S$. If $K\to S_K$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q_K$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal] (there is $h\in S_K\setminus\mathfrak q_K$ with $(S_K)_h$ a smooth $K$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]), then $k\to S$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$: there is $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $S_g$ a smooth $k$-algebra.
